I go to synagogue every Shabbat and we always say the same prayers — the Kaddish, the Shema — every single time. Most of the people I talk through serious decisions with are from that same community. Do you think relying on the same tight-knit group for most of your big decisions changes how much you trust yourself when they are not around?

What a thoughtful and introspective question. Relying on a tight-knit group, such as your synagogue community, for guidance and support can indeed have an impact on your self-trust, especially when faced with decisions outside of that community. On one hand, having a close-knit group can provide a sense of security and comfort, which can be beneficial in times of uncertainty. The familiarity and shared values within your community can help you feel more grounded and confident in your decision-making. The repetition of prayers and rituals, like the Kaddish and Shema, can also create a sense of continuity and connection to your community, which can be reassuring. On the other hand, relying too heavily on this group for decision-making can potentially undermine your self-trust when you're outside of that environment. If you're used to seeking guidance and validation from others within your community, you might feel less confident in your own abilities to make decisions when you're on your own or in unfamiliar situations. This phenomenon is often referred to as "external validation" versus "internal validation." When you rely on external validation from others, you may feel less inclined to trust your own instincts and judgment. This can lead to a sense of uncertainty or self-doubt when you're faced with decisions without the input of your community. To develop a stronger sense of self-trust, it's essential to strike a balance between seeking guidance from others and cultivating your own internal compass. Here are a few suggestions: 1. **Practice self-reflection**: Take time to reflect on your own values, goals, and priorities. Ask yourself what you truly believe in and what you stand for. 2. **Develop your critical thinking skills**: Learn to evaluate information, weigh pros and cons, and make decisions based on your own analysis. 3. **Take calculated risks**: Step out of your comfort zone and make decisions on your own, even if it feels uncomfortable at first. This will help you build confidence in your ability to make decisions without external input. 4. **Seek diverse perspectives**: While it's natural to seek guidance from your community, also try to expose yourself to different viewpoints and experiences. This can help you develop a more nuanced understanding of the world and increase your self-trust. 5. **Cultivate mindfulness and self-awareness**: Pay attention to your thoughts, emotions, and intuition. Recognize when you're seeking external validation and try to tap into your own inner wisdom. By working on these skills, you can develop a stronger sense of self-trust and become more confident in your ability to make decisions, even when you're outside of your community. Remember, it's okay to seek guidance from others, but it's also essential to trust yourself and your own abilities.
